lessons.title: Computing Tax on a Salary From Start to Finish

body.text: Your employer's TDS is only an estimate built on your salary. Your real tax is computed on everything you earned, and the gap between the two is what you settle, or get refunded, when you file.

children.text: Every piece of this course now comes together in one computation. We will follow one salaried employee from the CTC in her offer letter to the final rupee she pays or gets back, using every step you have learned: taxable salary, Total Income, slabs, rebate test, surcharge test, cess and TDS.

Deepika is a resident senior analyst at a multinational bank's technology centre in Bengaluru. She is 31, on the new regime for tax year 2026-27, and her offer letter shows a CTC of ₹25,00,000. She also earns ₹20,000 of savings account interest and ₹80,000 of interest on an FD with Canara Bank.

data.label: Taxable cash salary (basic, HRA, special allowance, bonus)

body.text: Employer contributions to PF, NPS and superannuation together are tax-free as salary only up to ₹7,50,000 a year. Deepika's employer PF of ₹1,20,000 and employer NPS of ₹1,40,000 total ₹2,60,000, well within the limit. For senior executives with very large retirement contributions, the excess becomes taxable.

body.caption: Deepika's Tax Computation, New Regime, Tax Year 2026-27

children.text: Total Income is rounded to the nearest multiple of ₹10 before the slabs are applied. The final tax, after cess, is also rounded to the nearest multiple of ₹10. So Total Income of ₹22,16,904 becomes ₹22,16,900, and tax of ₹2,64,394 becomes ₹2,64,390. Amounts ending in exactly 5 are rounded up. The ITR utility does both automatically.
What Has Already Been Paid: TDS
Deepika's employer deducts TDS from her salary every month. It projects her annual tax on salary alone, because she has not told HR about her interest income, and spreads that tax across the year.

body.latex: \text{Monthly TDS} \approx \frac{\text{Projected annual tax on salary} - \text{TDS already deducted this year}}{\text{Months remaining}}
body.caption: Employers recalculate as salary, bonuses and declarations change, so monthly TDS can vary

points: Canara Bank deducted 10% TDS on FD interest: ₹8,000
No TDS on savings account interest

cells: Less: TDS by Canara Bank on FD interest

children.text: The ₹17,996 gap is easy to explain with the marginal rate. Her ₹1,00,000 of interest sits in her 25% slab, so it attracts 26% tax with cess: ₹26,000. The bank deducted only ₹8,000, and nobody deducted anything on her savings interest. The remaining ₹18,000, less a few rupees of rounding, is left for her to pay.

body.text: Because Deepika's tax after TDS is ₹10,000 or more, she was liable to pay advance tax during the year. Paying the ₹17,996 only when she files her return means interest will be charged for the delay. There are two simple fixes. She can declare her interest income to her employer so it is included in salary TDS, or she can pay advance tax by the quarterly due dates.

body.title: Your Own Tax Computation Worksheet
steps: From your payslip or Form 16, list every salary component and mark which are taxable under your regime
Add the taxable components to get gross salary, then subtract the standard deduction
From AIS and your bank statements, add interest, dividends, rent and any other income, and split out special-rate income
Subtract the deductions your regime allows, such as the employer NPS contribution, and round Total Income to the nearest ₹10
Apply the slabs to slab-rate income and the special rates to special-rate income
Test the rebate (Total Income up to ₹12 lakh, new regime) and surcharge (above ₹50 lakh), and apply marginal relief if you are just above either
Add 4% cess, round to the nearest ₹10, then subtract all TDS, TCS and advance tax shown in Form 26AS
A positive balance is tax payable before filing; a negative balance is a refund

body.title: Manoj's Tax Liability
body.prompt: Manoj, a resident mechanical engineer at a Chennai auto plant, is on the new regime. His taxable gross salary is ₹14,75,000, his employer makes no NPS contribution, and he earns ₹10,000 of savings account interest. What is his total tax liability, including cess, before rounding?
body.explanation: Salary ₹14,75,000 less the ₹75,000 standard deduction is ₹14,00,000. Adding ₹10,000 of interest gives Total Income of ₹14,10,000. Slab tax is ₹60,000 + 15% of ₹2,10,000 = ₹91,500. No rebate, since income is above ₹12 lakh, and he is well past the marginal relief zone. Cess of ₹3,660 brings the total to ₹95,160, which is already a multiple of ₹10.

body.title: What Is Not Taxed This Year?
body.question: Under the new regime, which of these CTC components is normally not added to an employee's taxable salary for the year?
options: Performance bonus paid in the year
Employer's PF contribution at 12% of basic, within the ₹7.5 lakh combined limit
Employer's NPS contribution at 14% of basic
body.explanation: Employer PF within the combined limit is not taxable as salary. HRA is fully taxable under the new regime, and a bonus is taxable when paid. The employer NPS contribution is included in salary but then fully deducted, so it ends up not being taxed, but it does pass through the computation.

body.title: Paying the Balance
body.textWithBlank: Tax still due after TDS and advance tax, paid before filing the return, is called ___ tax.
body.explanation: Self-assessment tax is paid through the income tax portal before you file. The return cannot show a tax balance outstanding at filing, and any interest for delayed advance tax is added to it.

body.title: Priyanka's Surprise Bill
body.scenario: Priyanka, a resident UX researcher in Pune on the new regime, has taxable gross salary of ₹12,50,000 with no employer NPS. Her employer deducted no TDS all year, because her salary after the standard deduction is ₹11,75,000 and the rebate covers it. She also earned ₹60,000 of FD interest, on which her bank deducted ₹6,000 of TDS. She assumed she had no tax to pay.
body.prompt: Compute Priyanka's actual tax liability and the balance she owes. What could she have done differently?
body.modelAnswer: Total Income is ₹11,75,000 + ₹60,000 = ₹12,35,000, which is above ₹12 lakh, so there is no rebate. Slab tax is ₹60,000 + 15% of ₹35,000 = ₹65,250. She is inside the marginal relief zone: tax before cess is limited to the ₹35,000 excess over ₹12 lakh. With 4% cess her liability is ₹36,400. After the bank's ₹6,000 of TDS she owes ₹30,400. ₹60,000 of interest has cost her ₹36,400 in tax, because it pushed her out of the rebate. If her employer offers an NPS option, routing ₹35,000 of salary into employer NPS would have brought Total Income back to ₹12,00,000 and her tax to zero, with the bank's ₹6,000 TDS refunded. At minimum, she should have declared the FD interest to her employer so TDS matched her real liability.

cards.definition: Cost to company: everything the employer spends on you, including non-taxable items like employer PF and gratuity provisions.
The salary components taxable under your regime, before the standard deduction.
Tax deducted monthly by your employer, based on its projection of your annual tax on salary and any other income you declare.
The certificate your employer issues showing salary paid and TDS deducted for the year.
Tax paid in quarterly instalments during the year when tax after TDS is ₹10,000 or more.
Balance tax paid before filing the return, after TDS and advance tax.

points: Start from CTC, strip out non-taxable components, subtract the standard deduction and add other income to reach Gross Total Income
Subtract allowed deductions and round to the nearest ₹10 to get Total Income, then apply slabs and special rates
Test the rebate and surcharge against Total Income, apply marginal relief where relevant, add 4% cess and round tax to the nearest ₹10
Employer TDS usually covers only salary; interest, rent and gains often leave a balance at your marginal rate
A balance of ₹10,000 or more after TDS means advance tax was due, and paying late attracts interest
Declaring other income to your employer is the simplest way to avoid a surprise at filing time

body.text: The computation assumes a resident individual under the new regime for tax year 2026-27. Salary components and their tax treatment vary by employer. Interest for late advance tax is not calculated here. This lesson is for education only and is not tax advice.
